input: Find bootstrapped European vertical SaaS companies for logistics or freight with 50-200 employees

companies.name: Riege Software (Riege Software International GmbH)
companies.employees: About 131 (as_of 2025-06; cargoforwarder.eu article on the 40th anniversary refers to 'the other 131 Riege employees'). Source: https://cargoforwarder.eu/2025/06/09/riege-celebrated-its-40th-anniversary/

criteria_evidence.evidence: Release dated 2018-04-04 calls Riege a 'privately-owned and managed company' whose growth was funded internally rather than by outside investors. Founder Johannes Riege's sons run it and his wife Gabriele manages the finances.
Release dated 2025-05-20 says the company has been privately owned and managed since it was founded in 1985, with a second-generation CEO. No external investors are mentioned.
Releases are datelined Meerbusch, Germany (Meerbusch/Munich for the 40th-anniversary release).
Scope is cloud software for air freight, ocean freight and customs, used by freight forwarders and customs brokers. Early customers included Dachser and DB Schenker.

companies.headcount_growth: Only one dated employee count was found: 131 (as_of 2025-06). Company press materials say 120+ and 140+, but those PDFs could not be read, so no growth rate can be given. As a substitute, the customer count grew: 575+ (2021-04-13), 700+ (2024-11-28), 900+ (2025-05-20). Sources: https://www.riege.com/company/press/press-releases/10-years-riege-software-in-the-netherlands ; https://www.riege.com/company/press/press-releases/riege-software-grows-business-in-northern-europe
companies.last_round: None. Growth has been funded internally and there are no outside investors (as_of 2018-04-04; still described as privately owned on 2025-05-20). Source: https://www.riege.com/company/press/press-releases/riege-software-prepares-for-the-future-with-next-generation-taking-over
companies.traction: More than 900 customer companies in 60 countries (as_of 2025-05-20), up from more than 350 customers (as_of 2018-04-04). Source: https://www.riege.com/company/press/press-releases/40-years-of-riege-software-from-early-start-up-to-pacemaker-of-digital-logistics
companies.rank_reason: Best fit. The company itself says growth was funded internally with no outside investors. It is family-owned and run by the second generation, sells pure cloud SaaS for freight forwarding and customs, has 131 staff (inside 50-200), and its customer count has grown steadily.

companies.name: B2PWeb (B2P group)
companies.employees: 147 (as_of 2025; 154 in 2024; the company claims about 160 across the group). Source: https://blogistics.fr/annuaire/b2pweb/
companies.ownership: Owned by its users, not founders: H2P (Holding Premium Professionnel) is owned by 360 transport companies plus trade groupings and federations. No VC or PE.

criteria_evidence.evidence: No external funding rounds or investors are reported. The company is chaired by H2P, which is owned by 360 transport companies, and smaller firms have been able to buy in since September 2025 with a ticket of a few hundred euros. Share capital is €830,758.
HQ is 127 avenue Joseph Boitelet, 84300 Cavaillon, France.
Subscription freight exchange (bourse de fret) for road carriers and shippers. About 12,000 clients use the marketplace.
147 employees in 2025 and 154 in 2024. An earlier article (2023-04-13) gave about 150.

companies.headcount_growth: 154 (as_of 2024) to 147 (as_of 2025), about a 5% decline. About 150 (as_of 2023-04-13). Sources: https://blogistics.fr/annuaire/b2pweb/ ; https://www.vaucluse-entreprises.com/b2pweb-leader-francais-de-linnovation-dans-le-transport/
companies.last_round: No external round found. The only capital event is the opening of the shareholder base to small transport firms in September 2025. Source: https://blogistics.fr/annuaire/b2pweb/
companies.traction: Revenue of €19.5M with €1.19M net profit for the year ended 2025-06-30, up from €12.3M (2022), €13.2M (2023) and €16.1M (2024). Source: https://blogistics.fr/annuaire/b2pweb/
companies.rank_reason: Strong fit on self-funding, size (147), vertical freight SaaS and profitable growth (revenue up about 58% from 2022 to 2025). Ranked below Riege because its owners are a holding of industry users rather than a founder or family, and headcount fell slightly from 2024 to 2025.

companies.name: Transport Exchange Group Ltd (Courier Exchange / Haulage Exchange / Integra)
companies.hq: Nottingham, United Kingdom (registered office). Built In lists London as HQ, with offices in London and Nottingham.
companies.employees: 113 (Built In London profile, no date given). Source: https://builtinlondon.uk/company/transport-exchange-group

criteria_evidence.evidence: Companies House lists founder Lyall Roger Cresswell as the person with significant control, holding 75% or more of shares and voting rights and the right to appoint directors (notified 2016-04-06). No funding round was found.
UK private company 03464353, active, incorporated 1997-11-12, registered office Newstead House, Pelham Road, Nottingham, SIC 62090.

Road-freight technology company with a digital platform for the road transport supply chain, sold through the brands CX (Courier Exchange), HX (Haulage Exchange) and Integra, across the UK, Europe and North America.

companies.last_round: No funding round found. The founder holds 75% or more (Companies House PSC register). Source: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/03464353/persons-with-significant-control
companies.traction: Courier Exchange has 10,000+ members and the group reports more than 38,625 active users (company site, read 2026-11). Source: https://courierexchange.co.uk/about-us
companies.rank_reason: Companies House confirms founder control of 75% or more, and the business is a vertical freight-exchange SaaS. The headcount (113) fits but has no date, no second dated count was found, and a third-party snippet mentioning 'top investors' (page not readable) could not be checked, so it ranks below the two companies with stronger evidence.

companies.name: SPEDION GmbH
companies.ownership: founder-owned (managing directors Günter Englert and Wolfram Grohse hold 40% each)

criteria_evidence.evidence: Register data lists Günter Englert (40%) and Wolfram Grohse (40%) as shareholders and managing directors since 2003, plus one partly masked 10% holder and one further holder whose details are hidden. Registered capital is €25,000 and the company was registered on 2002-12-18. No VC or PE was found.
HQ at Industriestr. 7, 63829 Krombach, Germany. Founded March 2003.
Telematics and fleet software for freight carriers and transport companies: SPEDION App, SPEDIONline portal, Navigation, Tachodata and LUCY App, sold alongside its own hardware.

companies.last_round: No funding round found. A December 2012 shareholder change brought in a new partner for sales (the page could not be opened, so this is not verified). Ownership is shown at https://handelsregister.ai/de/organizations/krombach/speditionen/spedion-gmbh-ca6fbc11b6a4b05ee9abdb6779610dff
companies.traction: Over 300 customers and about 15,000 users (as_of 2018). Source: https://trendkraft.io/newsroom/spedion-gmbh
companies.rank_reason: Ownership by the two founder-managers is clearly documented and the company is vertical for road freight. It ranks last because it sells hardware alongside software (less pure SaaS), the headcount is only a 50-100 band, and the traction data is old (2018).

output.search_notes:
Only 4 companies passed every check: Riege Software, B2PWeb, Transport Exchange Group and SPEDION. Pages that returned errors are not cited.

EXCLUDED, external capital or not private:
- Mandata (UK): backed by LDC, then Tenzing.
- Ongoing Warehouse (SE): Cinven invested in 2026.
- Wtransnet (ES): sold to the fund Castik.
- Setlog (DE): bought by Rhenus in 2023.
- YellowFox (DE): majority previously held by ECM / GEP V, sold to Peter Möhrle in 2025, so not bootstrapped.
- Frotcom (PT): HCapital took a minority stake in 2018.
- EuroTracs (BE): bought by FleetGO, which is backed by Main Capital.
- CargoSoft (DE): a DAKOSY subsidiary.
- Opter (SE): listed on Nasdaq First North.
- Shipnet: owned by Volaris.
- Dataloy: acquired.
- Movertis (ES): merged into Movilia, backed by Seaya Andromeda.

EXCLUDED, outside 50-200 employees:
- Soloplan (DE): 250 staff in 2024, although family-run.
- LIS / WinSped (DE): more than 260 staff in a June 2026 report.
- Mapon (LV): over 200 staff, and Draugiem Group-owned.

NOT VERIFIED, so excluded:
- Boltrics (NL): about 50 staff; ownership not confirmed.
- TIS GmbH (DE): its own interview says it is no longer family-owned, and the current owner is unknown.
- Hogia Logistics (SE): a subsidiary of Hogia Group, and family ownership was not confirmed.

LIMITS:
- No company had two dated, verifiable employee counts except B2PWeb (154 in 2024, 147 in 2025).
- Riege's press-kit PDFs could not be read, so their 120+ and 140+ figures are not used.
- The Endole and Creditreform pages for Transport Exchange Group and SPEDION returned 403 errors.
- Transport Exchange Group: Companies House gives an incorporation date of 1997, but the company site says it was founded in 2000. The employee count of 113 has no date.
- B2PWeb's owner is a holding of transport firms rather than a founder. It is listed as bootstrapped because it has never taken VC or PE, which is a judgement call.
- Missing fields: Transport Exchange Group headcount_growth; SPEDION headcount_growth; Riege headcount_growth (only one dated count).
